text:
alex: Heads-up — infra-bot just flagged a spike of ECC errors on gpu-node-03 (us-west-2).
infra-bot: [ALERT] gpu-node-03 ecc_spike=12 xid_spike=4 severity=medium run_id=memcheck-1799991111
maya: Ugh, that node is in the pool for low-priority training jobs. Are we seeing evictions or just kernels throwing XID? :confused:
sam: Logs show repeated XID(43) + ECC counters incrementing. Not a single flaky CUDA panic yet, more like intermittent memory parity errors.
jin: Can we avoid a full cordon+drain immediately? We risk displacing a bunch of long-running jobs and burning preemptible capacity.
alex: Proposal: run targeted memtest on that node during a mini-drain window — mark it as "soft-isolated" so new jobs avoid it, run memtest via slurm's --nodelist and only fully drain if memtest fails.
maya: Agree. What's the command pattern? We should script it and run as a safety job.
sam: Example command I tested in staging:
```
srun --nodes=1 --nodelist=gpu-node-03 --exclusive --time=00:30:00 memtester 16G 5
```
If memtester returns non-zero -> escalate to full cordon+replace.
jin: Add a short cooldown so transient temperature/ECC bursts don't cause churn. Maybe require >= 3 ECC spikes in 1h OR memtest fail.
ops-oncall: Also want to make sure autoscaler doesn't immediately provision replacements and overcommit capacity. We should create an annotation like `infra.redwood/soft-isolate: true` and have the scaler respect it for 30m.
alex: Good point. Plan:
- infra-bot detects ecc threshold => create incident & label node: `soft-isolate`
- schedule memtest job (niced) with 30m timeout
- if memtest passes => clear label after 1h monitor window
- if memtest fails or more XIDs occur => cordon+drain and queue replacement
- notify slack + create JIRA ticket for swap/return-to-stock
maya: Slight tweak: if there are critical prod pods on it, run a canary eviction policy: migrate critical pods to a reserved small buffer instead of full eviction.
sam: Also capture nvml logs for postmortem:
```
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.errors.volatile.dbe,retired_pages.single_bit,retired_pages.double_bit --format=csv -f /tmp/gpu-node-03-ecc.csv
```
Attach that to the incident.
jin: What about cost? If memtest often passes after a reboot we might be reboots > replacements. Could we prefer soft-reboot first? Soft-reboot + memtest is cheaper than swap.
ops-oncall: yes, add step: if memtest fails => attempt graceful kernel reboot once (if node unschedulable) before RMA; but only if it has low RMA history.
alex: I'll write a small runbook and a PR to infra-bot rules to implement the flow. Short-term mitigation: add a 30m `soft-isolate` annotation to gpu-node-03 and schedule memtest job now.
infra-bot: Action queued: set label `infra.redwood/soft-isolate=true` on gpu-node-03; scheduling memtest job (memcheck-1799991111). Notifying oncall.
ops-oncall: Running memtest now. Will post results here.
maya: Thanks — also add a monitor to block autoscaler from adding replacement nodes for 15m while the memtest runs, to avoid capacity churn.
sam: If memtest passes, we should replay job load to ensure no regressions then let node rejoin with `reintegrate` tag.
jin: Sounds good. Keep the escalation threshold documented; avoid hard drains for single-spike ECCs.
ops-oncall: Memtest finished: memtester exit=1 -> errors detected. nvml export attached. Starting cordon+drain per policy.
alex: Acknowledge. Triggering replacement workflow and creating ticket: RMA request + swap schedule.
maya: Please also mark node with `hardware.rma=recommended` in asset DB.
infra-bot: Node cordoned and evicted. Replacement requested. Incident created: IN-1799991111. Logs uploaded.
sam: Thanks team. After we replace, let's run a weekly passive memcheck sweep for nodes that hit >5 ECC in 24h.
jin: I'll add that to the infra roadmap item. Closing loop once RMA confirmed.
ops-oncall: RMA scheduled for 2026-04-02. Will update once swapped.
alex: Great work, everyone. Short-term checklist created in runbook PR.
